finding: In India (rated restaurants), delivery outlets are more often High-popularity (44.6% vs 27.2%), but their mean rating is almost the same (3.37 vs 3.34): delivery goes with more votes, not better ratings. Delivery exists only in India and the UAE.

finding: Votes and rating are strongly linked (Spearman rho = 0.68). The target is built from votes, so votes, rating and anything derived from them are excluded from the model's features.
2,148 restaurants (22.5%) have no rating yet; only 4.5% of them offer online delivery, against 31.8% of rated ones.
The honest model (Gradient Boosting) reaches 61.3% accuracy against a 33.6% baseline. Location is its strongest signal: without location features accuracy falls to 51.9%.
Accuracy is 44.8% for restaurants within 5 percentile points of a class cut-off and 79.3% for those far from it. Telling High from Low alone (a separate, easier question) reaches 83.2%.
